title: Brother Lawrence's kitchen
hookLine: a monastery cook found God as near among the pots as at the altar

cards: A busy kitchen at dinner time. Pots boiling over. Somebody shouting for more bread, somebody else for the salt.
The floor is wet, the oven is too hot, and the cook has a limp and a bad back. Not exactly a holy place.
In a monastery in Paris, the cook was a clumsy former soldier who, by his own account, had a natural dislike of kitchen work. Yet visitors came away talking about his peace.
He said he felt God as near among the pots as in church.

teach.b: His name was Nicolas Herman. He grew up poor in France, and accounts of his life say he went for a soldier and was wounded. His faith first woke up, he said later, at eighteen, looking at a bare tree in winter.
Soon it would have leaves again, and flowers, and fruit. And all at once he felt the goodness and care of God.

teach.h: A LAY BROTHER IN THE KITCHEN.
teach.b: Years later he joined the Carmelites in Paris as a lay brother, taking the name Brother Lawrence. They put him in the kitchen for many years; later, when his leg got worse, he repaired sandals. He never wrote a book.
After he died, a friend gathered his few letters and notes of their conversations into a little collection, The Practice of the Presence of God.
Its idea is simple: talk to God all day, in plain words, not only at set times of prayer but while working. When the mind wanders, just come back, without fuss.
The time of work, he said, was no different to him from the time of prayer.
In the noise and clatter of the kitchen, with several people calling for different things at once, he felt God as calmly as if he were kneeling at the altar.

teach.h: THE OMELET, FOR LOVE OF GOD.
teach.b: He said he turned his little omelet in the pan for the love of God. When he'd finished, if there was nothing else to do, he'd pick up a straw from the floor, for love of God.
Benedict had asked his kitchen monk to treat the pots like altar vessels; Lawrence did it at the stove. Nothing heroic. Every small thing, done with God in the room.

how: Christians, Catholic and Protestant alike, read Brother Lawrence and try to turn to God briefly and often through the day, especially during chores and ordinary work.

games.q: you're praying in the kitchen and realize your mind wandered ten minutes ago. what does Brother Lawrence say to do?
o: come back to God simply, without fuss.
games.why: wandering is normal. you just turn back, plainly, and go on turning the omelet.

practice: Wash dishes as prayer, at a real sink or in your mind: the warm water, the soap, one plate at a time. With each dish, hold Brother Lawrence's thought that he was never working alone.
If you pray, say a word or two to God, plainly, as to someone standing beside you; if you don't, give one plate your full attention.
